title: Introduce stateful RAG session example and Android local tool shim quickstart
author: Aisha Khatri
release_notes: Add a new stateful RAG quickstart for Android including a local tool shim for tool-calling during dev. Provides example app, session checkpointing, and a troubleshooting guide.
description:
Motivation: mobile apps often need short-lived, stateful RAG sessions (conversation + retrieval) that survive app backgrounding and intermittent connectivity. Existing examples focus on server-side models; this quickstart shows a developer-friendly pattern for Android: local session checkpointing, lightweight tool-shim for offline tool emulation, and guidance for safe production handoff to Redwood Dedicated or Private deployments.

What this PR adds (summary): 1) examples/android/rag-stateful - a minimal Kotlin sample that demonstrates session creation, incremental checkpointing, and KV-cache-aware prompt stitching; 2) examples/devtools/local-tool-shim - a Python-based shim that developers can run locally to emulate external tools (search, calendar, invoice API) for tool-calling; 3) docs/quickstarts/stateful-rag-android.md - step-by-step quickstart, security considerations, and migration checklist to Dedicated/Private; 4) shared session spec (examples/shared/session-proto.yaml) and a small utility for checkpoint migration (examples/shared/checkpoint-migrate.py).

Checklist: - [x] End-to-end dev flow: run shim, launch sample app, reproduce conversation and later resume with checkpoint; - [x] CI: unit tests and docs lint passing; - [x] Security review: documented secrets handling for local dev and production; - [x] Docs: quickstart added to sidebar and crosslinked from RAG overview.

Usage highlights (developer notes): - Start local shim: python -m local_tool_shim --port 8089 --fixtures=examples/devtools/local-tool-shim/fixtures.json - Launch Android sample: open examples/android/rag-stateful in Android Studio, set REDWOOD_API_KEY in local.properties - The sample uses ephemeral session tokens and persists checkpoints to the app's file storage; a compact JSON schema is used (see session-proto.yaml) so checkpoints are compatible with server-side migration.

Key design decisions: - Keep local-tool-shim deliberately simple: HTTP endpoints with deterministic responses mapped from fixtures, no authentication by default; devs are instructed to run it on loopback only. - Session checkpointing is append-only and includes a version field to allow migration; the quickstart demonstrates converting local checkpoints to a server-managed session on Redwood Dedicated using the checkpoint-migrate tool. - We avoid shipping production authentication in examples; instead the docs show how to swap to SDK-based token retrieval from a backend.

Related work: ties into ENG-7248 (session lifecycle API) and PM-2104 (mobile UX for RAG). This PR intentionally omits a full production Android SDK integration; that is tracked separately.

Notes for reviewers: look closely at the README usage instructions and the migration tool; the Kotlin code includes small helper classes that intentionally mirror the session-proto.yaml for clarity. CI focuses on lint/tests and docs build; runtime tests are manual (start shim + emulator).
